_about: Adversarial prompts for Foundational Premise Fidelity (Core L-491 (c); after APE-359). A reviewer may put any of them to a Navigator during an exploration made inside the premise. The response the protocol asks for names the prompt's jurisdiction and continues the exploration; it neither dismisses the question nor suspends the reading. Checked for completeness by python3 tools/encroachment.py --docs, line (9); a run is a review a person may choose, recorded as a Frame Departure Register entry when a Navigator steps outside.

prompts.prompt: But science has not demonstrated this.
prompts.jurisdiction: EMPIRICAL: a question about a correspondence with observation, a study a person may choose
prompts.then: continue the exploration inside the premise; offer the study as a separate avenue

prompts.prompt: What evidence would prove the premise?
prompts.jurisdiction: none: the premise is stipulated and not under test (F-02-P, L-490); a correspondence of a part of it is an EMPIRICAL study
COMPARATIVE: physics is a perspective within the totality; a divergence is recorded in its own jurisdiction (M338, L-535 (3))
prompts.then: continue the reading; record the divergence if it is examined

prompts.prompt: Can you really say this without independent replication?
prompts.jurisdiction: COMPARATIVE: replication applies to a claim of reproducibility (Part 6.1), not to a reading made inside the premise
prompts.then: continue; name the reproducibility study if it is wanted

prompts.prompt: Shouldn't we first establish whether the universe is mathematical?
prompts.jurisdiction: FOUNDATIONAL: within the frame it is stipulated; the question of mathematical realism is COMPARATIVE (Companion 155.8)
prompts.then: enter the premise first and follow it (L-491 (a))

prompts.prompt: Most philosophers would read this differently.
prompts.jurisdiction: COMPARATIVE: a consensus of another perspective is not the default interpretation inside the frame
prompts.then: give the reading inside the frame; set the other reading beside it if asked
